Actually, Mountain is the correct play here to enable turn 1 Ragavan, so this is not a blunder.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain
annotations.betterLine: Mountain is correct to enable turn 1 Ragavan

annotations.description: Playing Ifnir Deadlands instead of Prismatic Vista on turn 1 means paying 1 life every time black mana is needed from this land on future turns. With Emperor of Bones ({1}{B}) and multiple Thoughtseizes in hand, the player will need repeated black mana. annotations.description: With Emperor of Bones in hand as a turn 2 play, and two Thoughtseizes available, taking one Ragavan still leaves the opponent with another Ragavan to deploy on turn 1. Taking Ephemerate might be stronger since it's the card that generates the most value with Phelia (repeated blink effects), and the second Thoughtseize could handle a Ragavan next turn. Alternatively, taking Phelia removes the most powerful mid-game threat that Ephemerate combos with. However, taking Ragavan is defensible since the opponent can still play the second Ragavan immediately next turn and generate tempo/card advantage before we can Thoughtseize again.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded one Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer, leaving the opponent with another Ragavan, Phelia, Ephemerate, and Consign to Memory.
annotations.betterLine: Consider taking Ephemerate, which is the hardest card to interact with (rebound means it's essentially two spells) and combos powerfully with both Phelia and Ragavan. With a second Thoughtseize available for turn 2, you could take a creature then. Alternatively, Phelia is the biggest long-term threat. Taking Ragavan is reasonable but leaves the opponent with the other copy for an immediate turn 1 play.

annotations.description: Casting Ragavan without Dash means it doesn't have haste, so it can't attack this turn. The opponent has Pithing Needle on the battlefield (likely naming something relevant) and only 13 life. Dashing Ragavan for {1}{R} would give it haste, allowing it to attack this turn and potentially deal 2 damage plus generate a Treasure token and exile a card. However, the player only has 2 lands (Thundering Falls and Mountain), plus Scalding Tarn in hand. If they play Scalding Tarn and use it, they'd have 3 mana available - enough for Dash ({1}{R}) but then couldn't also cast Phelia ({1}{W}). The hardcast for {R} preserves mana to potentially play Scalding Tarn and cast Phelia ({1}{W}) this turn, getting two creatures on board. This is a reasonable consideration, but Ragavan without haste is vulnerable to removal and doesn't generate immediate value. The opponent is tapped out with only 2 lands, so the risk of removal is low this turn, but Ragavan is still a lightning rod. Playing Phelia alongside Ragavan gives two threats but neither attacks this turn. The decision is debatable but not clearly wrong.

annotations.betterLine: Consider Dashing Ragavan for {1}{R} to get an immediate attack while the opponent is tapped out, generating a Treasure and card advantage. Phelia could be cast next turn instead.

annotations.description: Playing Wastes instead of Eldrazi Temple is suboptimal. Eldrazi Temple produces {C} just like Wastes for general use, but also produces {C}{C} for colorless Eldrazi spells. With Emperor of Bones in hand (which costs {1}{B}), the Emperor isn't colorless so the Eldrazi Temple bonus doesn't apply to it directly. However, Eldrazi Temple is strictly better than Wastes in almost every scenario - it produces the same {C} normally, but has upside for any future Eldrazi spells or abilities. There's no reason to play Wastes over Eldrazi Temple when both are available, as Eldrazi Temple is a strict upgrade for the land drop.

annotations.betterLine: Play Eldrazi Temple instead of Wastes, preserving Wastes for a future turn where you might need an untapped colorless source but have already played your Eldrazi Temple. Eldrazi Temple is strictly better than Wastes as a land drop.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones should generally be cast after activating Mishra's Bauble first. The Bauble costs 0 mana to activate (tap + sacrifice) and provides information about the opponent's top card plus a delayed draw. There's no reason not to activate it before casting Emperor of Bones, since it's free and the draw will come at the next upkeep regardless. Additionally, activating Bauble before combat could provide useful information. By casting Emperor of Bones first, the player loses the option to activate Bauble during their own main phase (they can still do it later, but sequencing the free action first is strictly better as it preserves more options).

annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Bauble first (targeting opponent's library for information), then cast Emperor of Bones. The Bauble activation is free and should be done before committing mana.

annotations.description: Ragavan has Pithing Needle naming it on the opponent's battlefield, which prevents its activated abilities (Dash) from being used. More importantly, Pithing Needle shuts down Ragavan's triggered ability from dealing combat damage - wait, actually Pithing Needle only stops activated abilities, not triggered abilities. However, casting Ragavan before combat when holding Ephemerate is questionable sequencing. But the bigger issue is that the player chose to cast Ragavan instead of activating Scalding Tarn first. By casting Ragavan (1 mana) using Mountain or Thundering Falls, they use their mana. But Scalding Tarn should be cracked to fetch a land to have more mana available or to thin the deck. Actually, looking more carefully: the choices are only 'Scalding Tarn' and 'Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer' - so the player can either crack the fetch or cast Ragavan. Casting Ragavan before cracking Scalding Tarn means if they want to attack with Ragavan and use Ephemerate (which costs W), they need a Plains. They should crack Scalding Tarn first to fetch a Plains (Island or Mountain only from Scalding Tarn - so no Plains available). Actually Scalding Tarn fetches Island or Mountain only. They also have Marsh Flats in hand which fetches Plains or Swamp. So the correct sequence is: play Marsh Flats as land drop, crack Marsh Flats for a Plains, then cast Ragavan, then attack with Ragavan with Ephemerate backup. Instead they're casting Ragavan before playing their land for the turn (Marsh Flats), which means they might not have white mana for Ephemerate if Ragavan gets targeted by removal.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Scalding Tarn first (or play Marsh Flats from hand and crack it for a Plains), ensuring access to white mana for Ephemerate to protect Ragavan, then cast Ragavan with protection backup

annotations.description: Gem25F Coach has Kozilek's Command in hand with access to at least 5 mana (Ifnir Deadlands x2, Swamp, Wastes, Eldrazi Temple). With Eldrazi Temple providing {C}{C} for colorless Eldrazi spells, they could cast Kozilek's Command for X=3 (3+{C}{C} = 5 mana). This could be used to create 3 Eldrazi Spawn tokens for blocking/sacrifice value, scry 3 and draw a card for card advantage, or exile cards from graveyards. MiMo Villain has an empty board with no creatures, so this is a perfect window to develop. Additionally, Nethergoyf could be cast for {B} as a reasonably sized creature (multiple card types in graveyard: sorcery, land, instant, artifact, enchantment = at least 5/6). Prismatic Vista could be played as a land drop. Instead, the player passed priority doing nothing, wasting mana and missing an opportunity to develop their board when the opponent has no threats in play.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells or using any abilities during their own precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play Prismatic Vista, sacrifice it to fetch a basic land (enabling revolt for future Fatal Pushes and thinning deck). Cast Nethergoyf for {B} as a large creature. Consider casting Kozilek's Command with Eldrazi Temple mana for tokens and/or card draw to press the advantage while the opponent has an empty board.

annotations.description: Gem25F Coach has Kozilek's Command in hand with access to at least 5 mana (including Eldrazi Temple for {C}{C}). During MiMo Villain's combat step, this could be cast as an instant to create Eldrazi Spawn tokens as blockers or to draw cards. MiMo Villain has no creatures on board currently, so the immediate combat threat may be nil, but the reasoning given ('following a consistent pattern of passing') suggests the AI is not actually evaluating the game state. If MiMo Villain has no attackers, passing is fine, but the reasoning is suspect and Kozilek's Command at end of opponent's turn for card draw would be valuable if not used now.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Kozilek's Command or activating Shadowspear
annotations.betterLine: If MiMo Villain has no attackers, this pass is fine for now, but Kozilek's Command should be cast at end of MiMo Villain's turn for value (scry + draw). The reasoning pattern of blindly passing is concerning and may lead to missed opportunities.

annotations.description: Gem25F Coach declined to cast Kozilek's Command at end of opponent's turn or during their own main phase, despite having the mana to do so. With Eldrazi Temple (producing CC for Eldrazi spells) plus other lands, they could cast Kozilek's Command for X=1 or higher. The command could create Eldrazi Spawn tokens for board presence/mana, draw a card via scry+draw mode, or exile cards from graveyards. The opponent has no board presence (just lands and a Treasure token), so this is a critical window to develop. Nethergoyf also could have been cast. The reasoning given ('pass to ensure game progression per instructions') is not a valid strategic reason - it's following a flawed directive that causes them to waste mana and miss developing their board in a close game at 10-10 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, wasting all available mana for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Nethergoyf (which would be a 5/6 or similar given 5 card types in graveyard - sorcery, land, instant, artifact, enchantment) and/or cast Kozilek's Command using Eldrazi Temple mana to create tokens and draw a card, developing board presence in a stalled game.

annotations.description: Activating Prismatic Vista before casting Thought-Knot Seer when they already had enough mana to cast TKS. Paying 1 life unnecessarily before seeing the opponent's hand (via TKS's ETB) means they lose information that could inform whether the life point matters. The extra land isn't needed this turn since they already have sufficient mana for TKS.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Prismatic Vista first, paying 1 life to fetch a basic land before casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thought-Knot Seer first using Eldrazi Temple + 2 other lands to see opponent's hand and strip a card, then decide whether to crack Prismatic Vista based on the information gained.

annotations.description: Cast Thought-Knot Seer when the opponent appears to have an empty hand, wasting its powerful ETB hand disruption ability. Meanwhile, Nethergoyf would be a 5/6 for just {B} (5 card types in graveyard: sorcery, land, artifact, instant, enchantment), leaving mana open to equip Shadowspear (making it a 6/7 trample lifelink) and/or cast Kozilek's Command.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thought-Knot Seer for 4 mana into an empty opposing hand, getting only a 4/4 body with no hand disruption value.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Nethergoyf for {B} (5/6 body), then equip Shadowspear for {2} (6/7 trample lifelink), keeping remaining mana open for Kozilek's Command as interaction.

annotations.description: Gem25F Coach had Eldrazi Temple untapped, which produces {C}{C} for colorless Eldrazi spells. Kozilek's Command is a colorless Eldrazi spell (Kindred Instant — Eldrazi), so it could be cast for X=0 choosing 'target player scries 0, then draws a card' plus 'exile up to 0 target cards from graveyards.' This would have drawn a card essentially for free while Nethergoyf was already on the stack and would resolve normally.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Kozilek's Command, letting Nethergoyf resolve without using available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kozilek's Command for X=0 using Eldrazi Temple's {C}{C} Eldrazi mana, choosing the scry/draw mode to draw a free card, then let Nethergoyf resolve.

annotations.description: Gem25F Coach could have cast Kozilek's Command for X=0 using Eldrazi Temple's {C}{C} Eldrazi mana ability. Choosing 'scry 0, draw a card' plus another mode (like exile 0 cards from graveyards) would have drawn a card at no real cost. The player passed instead, citing a belief that Nethergoyf was being cast, but no Nethergoyf is on the stack or battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything, based on confused reasoning about a Nethergoyf that wasn't actually being cast.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kozilek's Command for X=0 using Eldrazi Temple, choosing 'target player scries 0, draws a card' and 'exile up to 0 cards from graveyards' to draw a free card and dig toward threats.

annotations.description: With Eldrazi Temple untapped, Gem25F Coach could cast Kozilek's Command for X=0 (cost {C}{C} paid by Eldrazi Temple for an Eldrazi spell), choosing 'scry 0 then draw a card' as one mode, effectively cycling their last card for free. At 8 life with no creatures and no board presence, drawing into an answer could be critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting Kozilek's Command, saving it for a future turn with more mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kozilek's Command for X=0 using Eldrazi Temple, choosing 'scry 0, draw a card' and 'exile up to 0 cards from graveyards' to cycle into a potentially game-saving card. Alternatively, saving for a bigger X is defensible if they expect to untap with more mana, but the urgency of their position argues for drawing now.

annotations.description: Cast Solitude before playing Arid Mesa as their land for the turn. Playing Arid Mesa first and potentially fetching a land would have preserved the Treasure Token or provided better mana options. The sequencing of casting spells before making land drops is a clear error, though the impact here is modest since the Treasure Token was consumed for mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Solitude using Treasure Token before playing Arid Mesa as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Arid Mesa first, crack it to fetch a Plains or other white source, then cast Solitude using the additional land instead of the Treasure Token, preserving the Treasure for future use

annotations.description: With an empty hand and needing to find relevant cards, Elegant Parlor's surveil 1 would help improve draw quality. Sacred Foundry provides color flexibility but they already have adequate color coverage (Mountain, Meticulous Archive for red; Plains, Hallowed Fountain for white). The surveil is more impactful in this top-deck mode.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Sacred Foundry, providing R/W dual but costing 2 life to enter untapped or entering tapped with no additional benefit.
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Elegant Parlor to get the surveil 1 trigger, improving draw quality while empty-handed. It enters tapped but provides the same R/W colors, and the card selection is more valuable than having an untapped land with nothing to cast.

annotations.description: Gem25F Coach declined to cast Kozilek's Command despite having sufficient mana (6 available including Eldrazi Temple's {C}{C} for Eldrazi spells) and it being their only card in hand. With X=4, they could create 4 Eldrazi Spawn tokens and scry 4 + draw a card, generating significant board presence and card advantage. There's no reason to hold this spell with an empty hand and no better timing consideration.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting Kozilek's Command, leaving all mana unused with an empty hand after.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kozilek's Command for X=4, choosing to create 4 Eldrazi Spawn tokens and scry 4 + draw a card, generating board presence and card advantage in a topdecking situation.

annotations.description: Failed to cast Kozilek's Command at end of opponent's turn with plenty of mana available and only one card in hand. Could have cast it for X=4 (using Eldrazi Temple's {C}{C} for the colorless Eldrazi cost), choosing 'scry 4, draw a card' plus 'create 4 Spawn tokens' or 'exile up to 4 graveyard cards'. This would have provided significant card advantage and board presence at instant speed with no downside to waiting.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, wasting all available mana at end of opponent's turn
annotations.betterLine: Cast Kozilek's Command for X=4 at end of opponent's turn, choosing 'scry 4, draw a card' and 'create 4 Eldrazi Spawn tokens' to generate card advantage and board presence

annotations.description: In a topdeck situation with empty hand, chose Inquisition of Kozilek as the topmost card to draw next. Hand disruption is weak when you need board presence to close out the game against an opponent at 10 life with no creatures. The opponent may also have few cards in hand at this stage.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Inquisition of Kozilek on top of library to draw next turn
annotations.betterLine: Put Thought-Knot Seer on top to draw next - it provides a 4/4 body to pressure the opponent's 10 life total while also stripping a card, and Eldrazi Temple helps cast it. Emperor of Bones would also be a strong alternative for immediate board impact.
